turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How can I tell if a restaurant is good before I go?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Read the most recent reviews rather than the overall score. Look for comments about specific dishes, not just the service.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about photos?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Customer photos are more honest than the restaurant's own. If the food looks the same across many photos, the kitchen is consistent.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And I always wonder / whether a short menu is a good sign.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Usually yes. A short menu often means fresher ingredients and dishes the kitchen has really mastered.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good to know. I'll stop avoiding those places.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You might find some favorites. Small menus are often where the best cooking happens.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm eating out alone for the first time tonight and it feels a little awkward.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lots of people enjoy solo dining. Sitting at the bar or a counter feels very natural, and you can chat with the staff.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I bring a book?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure, a book or a podcast is totally normal. Or just people-watch, that's half the fun.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I was thinking of going to / that ramen place downtown.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ramen is ideal for solo dining. Many ramen shops are built around counters, and the meals are quick.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, maybe I'll do the Italian place instead, I want to linger.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Also a great choice. Order a glass of wine and take your time with every course.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is it rude to ask for the check right after we finish eating?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not at all, especially if the restaurant is busy. A simple, could we get the check when you have a moment, is perfectly polite.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about splitting the bill between five people?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Tell the server at the start of the meal if you can. It makes things much easier for them at the end.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And how much should we / tip for a big group?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: In the United States, eighteen to twenty percent is standard. Some places add it automatically for groups of six or more, so check the bill first.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, I didn't know that. Good thing I asked.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It catches a lot of people out. Otherwise you might accidentally tip twice.

option_sets.lead_in: I'm picking a place for my team dinner on Friday, can you help?
options: The first one is an Italian place downtown, great pasta, but it's quite noisy on weekends.
Then there's a sushi restaurant near the office with private rooms, but it's pretty expensive.
And the last one is a casual barbecue joint with long picnic tables and a big patio.
moshi_comment: For a team dinner, the sushi place's private rooms are a big plus, everyone can talk without shouting. The barbecue joint is cheaper and more relaxed if the weather is nice. What's the budget per person?
I'd lean toward the barbecue place, long tables are perfect for a group and the vibe is easygoing. The Italian spot sounds tasty, but noise on a Friday could make conversation hard.

option_sets.lead_in: My sister's birthday dinner is next week, and I have to choose where we go.
options: First, there's a rooftop bar with small plates and an amazing view of the river.
Second, a family-run Mexican restaurant where the staff sing to you on your birthday.
There's also a fancy French bistro she's mentioned wanting to try for ages.
Or lastly, we could just do a pizza night at my place with the whole family.
moshi_comment: If she's been wanting to try the French bistro for ages, that would feel really thoughtful. The Mexican place is more fun if she enjoys a bit of attention. Does she like being the center of attention?
The rooftop bar sounds special, but small plates can leave people hungry at a birthday dinner. I'd pick the French bistro, and save pizza night for a relaxed family weekend.
